nodes.description: The payload of one story point report (23 §5 'Local story point/report'): story point key, occurrence id, run and exact release, outcome and the observed game revision. It names no account (authentication supplies it) and no evidence class (only the server assigns one, 23 §6).

The server enforces that an account binding and release never change after registration (23 §5).
nodes.name: StoryRun

nodes.description: A Story run/save lineage (23 §5; 03 §25). A semantic restore or fork is a new run (23 §11). Lowercase hyphenated UUID, any version.
nodes.name: StoryRunId

nodes.description: One source's contribution to an actor's ActionSet (06 §19; ADR-016), applied to the set composed so far by stable action key: union adds the named actions whose keys the set lacks, override adds them and replaces those it has, replace makes the set exactly them, subtract removes them and intersect keeps only them. A key names an engine verb (a registered command type), a cartridge action or a cartridge recipe; union, override and replace take its definition (a cartridge's own over the engine verb's). A room applies its contributions in order after the engine verbs and the cartridge's actions and recipes (kernel/ts/src/actions.ts).
nodes.name: ActionContribution

nodes.description: An advertised affordance (04 §19; 06 §20; 21 §7): stable key, localization label, target spec, the portable Command type it resolves to (checked against the command registry when content compiles), presentation priority, required input parameters, policy and accessibility description. Aliases, costs and cooldown hints arrive with the text parser and cost capabilities.
nodes.name: ActionDefinition

nodes.description: The validated input of an ActionInvocation (04 §1). Closed: each field is a registered input parameter, and the ActionDefinition's `input` lists which ones the action requires (06 §20). The parameters are those the R6P proof uses (pre-release-proof.md).
nodes.name: ActionInput

nodes.description: An input parameter an action requires (06 §20), one of the ActionInput fields.
nodes.name: ActionInputParameter

nodes.description: A host-neutral gameplay intent from an advertised GameView action; not yet an authoritative Command (04 §1, §2). invocation_id is the stable retry identity (03 §14). target_ids is ordered and its order is semantic (03 §14, invocation-intent digest). view_freshness_token is opaque admission metadata, not intent (04 §16). The 8-target and 128-character caps are admission limits of this contract version (not spec numbers); changing them is a contract version change.
nodes.name: ActionInvocation

nodes.description: A cartridge-local action composed only of registered operations (06 §20 Composed actions / ActionRecipe; 21 §7; 05 §28), invoked by the perform command: its stable key (its ActionSet identity), label, the aliases a player types as its verb (the first words of the command), its target, presentation priority, availability policy (evaluated for the actor; while it fails the action is shown unavailable and perform is rejected), and its outcomes. success is one explicit sequence of at most 16 steps, run in order as one logical decision (04 §5.2) and followed by the engine's action_completed event, and the narration its actor reads; observers is the line others in the room would read, kept for the first host with a second viewer. Optional (R5 S6): a check (RecipeCheck; check@1), whose result selects the outcome: success when it passes, failure when it fails; a recipe has a failure outcome exactly when it has a check (OUTCOME_MISMATCH). A failed check is an accepted perform with outcome failure whose RNG draw and time commit like success (04 §5.0); a recipe without a check has outcome performed. failure's sequence may be empty. duration, a whole number of LogicalTime units, advances the clock by that much on every accepted perform, success or failure (21 §7 Cost, time; 04 §5.4: one time.advance after the outcome's steps); events keep the time the perform was admitted at. action_completed follows the outcome's steps when the outcome is performed or success, never failure. Optional (R5 S6b): costs (RecipeCost, resource@1), paid in order by the actor's body on every admitted perform, failure included; one it cannot pay rejects the perform insufficient_resource before any check or draw. cooldown, a whole number of LogicalTime units: a perform by the same actor before the last admitted attempt's time plus cooldown is rejected cooldown; an admitted attempt, failure included, starts it at its admission time (delta cooldown.start), and at exactly that time plus cooldown the recipe is available again. Admission order: target, cooldown, costs, then the check. Result bands join later.
nodes.name: ActionRecipe

nodes.description: A stable semantic key: lowercase snake_case of at most 64 characters, the DefinitionRef segment rule (03 §2). Used for action keys, directions, choices, outcomes and key-valued facts.
nodes.name: Key

nodes.description: An entity a recipe's narration names, by the field its role selects (like entity.schema.json ItemLocation): an NPC or item of this cartridge, or the command's actor (its body). The loader reports an npc or item that names no definition of that kind in this cartridge as UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE.
nodes.name: NarrationParticipant

nodes.description: An ActionRecipe's Check (21 §7 Check; 00a `check: {kind: luck, chance: 50}`), owned by check@1: resolved once per admitted perform, after every admission check (a rejection draws nothing) and before any outcome step. luck draws one uniform integer in [0, 100) from the world's RNG (rng.ts uniform; xoshiro128ss-1.1, numeric profile) and passes when it is below chance; the draw commits whether the check passes or fails (04 §5.0). key names the check in its check_passed or check_failed event (a DefinitionRef of kind check in the cartridge's namespace), the key a quest objective matches (00a). An inline check's key is its check definition's key, so two recipes' checks may not share one (DUPLICATE_DEFINITION). ActionRecipe.check is this luck shape or a threshold (R5 S6b; see ActionRecipe). Modifiers, opposed checks and result bands join as further kinds and fields (result bands as more outcomes keys).
nodes.name: RecipeCheck

nodes.description: One resource cost of an ActionRecipe (21 §7 Cost): the actor's body pays amount of a resource of the cartridge on every admitted perform, failure included (04 §5.0). A perform whose body cannot pay (current value minus amount below the resource's minimum) is rejected insufficient_resource before any RNG draw, and changes nothing.
nodes.name: RecipeCost

nodes.description: A recipe outcome's narration (21 §4 NarrationSpec): the actor's line, the observers' line, and the entities the actor's line names, each resolved and pinned when the outcome commits (06 §43; text.schema.json Text participants).
nodes.name: RecipeNarration

nodes.description: One registered operation of a recipe outcome's explicit sequence (04 §5.2 step 4, §5.3; 05 §28: never a generic setter or an untyped effect). fact.assign sets a declared fact of the cartridge, at the one scope the fact allows, to a value of its type (the host emits fact_changed at this step's causal position when the value changes, fact@1). event.emit emits the cartridge's custom event of this key (EventPayload custom_event, action_recipe@1), whose subject is the recipe's target. resource.adjust adds by (negative: subtracts) to a resource of the actor's body, chained after the costs and any earlier adjust of it, stopping at the resource's bounds (DikuMUD-style: healing at full health heals nothing); this saturation is the step's declared meaning, not a silent clamp (04 §5.1): the rule computes the stopped value and proposes an exact delta resource.adjust to it, or none when the value does not change. Costs never saturate (RecipeCost).
nodes.name: RecipeStep

nodes.description: What an ActionRecipe acts on (06 §20 target; 21 §7 TargetSpec): here, one inspectable detail, by its room and its key in that room's details. The recipe is offered only while the actor is in that room; other target kinds (items, entities by property) join as further variants.
nodes.name: RecipeTarget

nodes.description: The deterministic result of resolving a target (14 §R3A; 21 §7: none | unique(target) | ambiguous(candidates), no random tie-breaking; 04 §18: ambiguous search returns structured candidates). candidate_ids are 2 to 1024 distinct EntityIds (1024 is the composition profile's selector_cardinality) in ascending code-point order of the id string (owner decision: docs/archive/decisions/owner-decisions-r3-open-questions-2026-09-24.md, item 1). The subset cannot express order or distinctness, so invariant target_candidates_ordered in protocol/invariants.json carries it.
nodes.name: TargetResolution

nodes.description: The candidate scopes an action's target is resolved from (21 §7): the scopes the R6P proof resolves to an EntityId. Inspectable details use target-only EntityIds and the inspectable_details scope. equipped, connections, party and privileged global scope are added with their first use, with a target identity for non-entity targets (21 §6). Accepted kinds and capabilities are added with the capability registry.
nodes.name: TargetSpec

nodes.description: A capability key (05 §6), lowercase snake_case, at most 64 characters. A capability contract is key@version.
nodes.name: CapabilityKey

nodes.description: The exact capability lock of a compiled cartridge or deployment (05 §3 'Compatibility versions', §6, §11): every capability version it executes. capability_lock_hash (09 §21) is hash(lock) under loka-numeric-v1; format is the hash domain tag, and any change to this format takes a new tag. Resolving a manifest's requirements and registry dependencies into a lock is the compiler's job (R4).
nodes.name: CapabilityLock

nodes.description: One registry entry (05 §6): a capability version, its portability, and its semantic residency from the residency matrix (05 §6 'Capability semantic residency matrix'). Portability limits residency (this table is the PM's adopted reading of 05 §6, not spec text): a portable capability is a portable semantic foundation or portable capability implementation, server_only is a Realm-only semantic capability, client_presentation_only is client presentation; authority-host coordination and authoring/certification are never capabilities (05 §6). A null residency is not yet classified. An Effect names the capabilities that may emit it (allowed_origins in protocol/effect_registry.json). A capability lists the commands, events and policy ops it owns (05 §6: a capability owns the commands, events and policies it introduces); each registered one has exactly one owning capability key, checked in test/loka/core/registries_test.exs. 04 §5 routes a choice to the capability that opened it; single static ownership is revisited when scene/quest choices arrive (R7). Only the portable branch has these fields for now; a server_only capability gains them with the first command, event or op it owns.
nodes.name: CapabilitySpec

nodes.description: A capability contract version (05 §6): a positive integer. key@version is immutable in meaning once published; a breaking change takes a new version (05 §6, 'Capability version immutability').
nodes.name: CapabilityVersion

nodes.description: Exact capability pins, capability key to version (05 §3 requires.capabilities; 05 §6). A map, so one version per key: the canonical decoder rejects a repeated key, and canonical encoding sorts keys.
nodes.name: CapabilityVersions

nodes.description: The six responsibility classes of the 05 §6 residency view ('Capability semantic residency matrix'). A capability's residency is one of the other four (CapabilitySpec); authority-host coordination and authoring/certification are never capabilities and appear only as Responsibility rows.
nodes.name: ResidencyClass

nodes.description: A row of the 05 §6 residency view that is not a registered capability (protocol/residency.json): a portable semantic foundation contract that both kernels must implement with golden cross-host parity, or a host or authoring responsibility named in 05 §6's 'Owns' column. fixtures lists the conformance files both kernels are tested against; an empty list means none is bound yet, never that none is needed. Host services are not made into gameplay capabilities by appearing here (05 §6).
nodes.name: Responsibility

nodes.description: One authored character choice and its bounded initial effects.
nodes.name: AncestrySpec

nodes.description: The byte length of a cartridge artifact file, checked before decoding: at most 4 MiB (owner decision, docs/archive/decisions/owner-decisions-r4-2026-09-25.md, item 2). bin/contracts.exs emits the maximum into kernel/ts/src/contracts.gen.ts as ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES; Elixir reads it here.

nodes.description: attributes@1 (00 §4.3 and 06 §21 amendments 2026-10-03): an attribute and its starting value, content and never an engine default. Every actor's value is start while nothing writes attributes (no state). In source, attributes.json's {"attributes": {key: {start}}}, the key taken from the map (an authored key is UNKNOWN_FIELD).

nodes.description: The semantic payload a cartridge hash covers (05 §11 'Hash domains and attestations'): the manifest with its compatibility requirements, the exact capability lock (exactly requires.capabilities until a registry dependency exists; the loader rejects a difference with LOCK_MANIFEST_MISMATCH), and the normalized definitions of the frozen kinds, each map keyed by DefinitionRefString so canonical key order orders it. A key's cartridge_id and cartridge_version are the manifest's id and version and its last segment is the definition's key; the compiler guarantees this and the loader rejects a mismatch (ARTIFACT_DEFINITION_KEY_MISMATCH); the subset cannot express it. format is the hash domain tag and selects the variant. Compatibility (PM ruling, R5 S1 review A7/F3): adding an OPTIONAL field to an existing definition kind, or an optional new definition map, keeps the tag, because an artifact without it keeps its bytes, hash and meaning; a change in the meaning or requirement of an existing field (a field made required, removed or reinterpreted) takes a new tag. Loaders stay fail-closed: an older loader rejects a field it does not know as UNKNOWN_FIELD, and kernel_api ranges govern which loader a cartridge needs. No certificate, signature, package or catalog field belongs here (CAR-10). In R4 the authored cartridge.json is exactly the CartridgeManifest object form (kernel_api as {at_least, below}, capabilities as key to version); the string forms (">=1.3 <2.0", key@version) are not accepted yet.

Every host serializes an equivalent command to the same canonical bytes (04 §21). nodes.description: The registered Command types; an unknown type fails before game rules (04 §3). Invocation-derived types carry the actor; run_job is authority-internal (04 §1) and is never built from a client invocation. These are the types the R6P proof uses (pre-release-proof.md).

nodes.description: What a pure decision returns (04 §5). accepted: a provisional proposal (delta, proposed events, effects, next RNG) with a typed outcome, including an admitted attempt that failed in game terms (04 §5.0). rejected: not admitted; consumes no RNG, time or cost (04 §5.0). fault: budget, conflict or evaluator fault; the whole proposal is discarded, so it carries none (04 §5.2 step 7). narration, when the attempt has any, is the required narration the host commits with the result and the receipt replays (04 §5.2 step 7; 06 §43); absent means none. Its 64-line cap is an admission limit of this contract version, not a spec number; output_bytes in the composition profile bounds the whole result. Projection hints arrive with GameView.

Receive is never combined with accept/hand_over. API1.7 fact.adjust applies a safe integer amount to a declared bounded integer fact using checked addition then authored bounds, lowered to fact.assign.

nodes.description: A DomainEvent, created from IdSource (01 A8). Lowercase hyphenated UUID, any version.
nodes.name: EventId

nodes.description: The registered event types (04 §8) the R6P proof uses (pre-release-proof.md). A cartridge's custom events are one type, custom_event, named by a DefinitionRef in the cartridge's namespace, so content never emits an engine-owned type (05 §28).
nodes.name: EventPayload

nodes.description: A typed, namespaced fact declaration (03 §7): key (the fact's DefinitionRef is cartridge@version:fact/key; the cartridge is the namespace, 05 §4), versioned type, default, allowed scope kinds (a set) and meaning. Transition constraints and the reference graph are added with the compiler (R4).

examples.meaning: Whether the missing child was found.

nodes.name: FactSpec

nodes.description: A fact's value type and default (03 §7). The types chapter one declares (00a §6): bool, enum over Keys, and int with optional inclusive bounds. The value itself is a FactValue (delta.schema.json).
nodes.name: FactType

nodes.description: One stored fact value (03 §13): unique by fact, scope and subject_id within its world context, the same identity as the fact MutationTarget (delta.schema.json). An unset fact has its FactSpec default and no record. Revision and timestamps are host persistence metadata, not portable state.
nodes.name: ScopedFact

nodes.description: Kind and schema version of one feature value (14 §R3B). The kind's freeze milestone adds its versioned fields here, as a oneOf branch per kind; before that, any other property is invalid.
nodes.name: FeatureEnvelope

nodes.description: One R3B feature kind (14 §R3B). Exactly the kinds in protocol/feature_registry.json, which gives each one's spec section and freeze milestone; unknown kinds are invalid. A reference to a feature definition is a DefinitionRef whose kind is one of these values (05 §4).
nodes.name: FeatureKind

nodes.description: One entry of protocol/feature_registry.json: a kind, the spec section that defines it, and the milestone that freezes its fields (14 §R3B).
nodes.name: FeatureRegistryEntry

nodes.description: One action of a resolved ActionSet (04 §19), for the entity or place it is listed under, with what the client needs to build its ActionInvocation (04 §2, §17) without a handwritten per-action catalog: the target spec (implicit entity targets name the entity an action is listed under; concrete target_ids name the exact targets, including Read place actions aimed at inspectable details) and the input parameters it requires, both from its ActionDefinition (action.schema.json). Lists are in presentation order, highest priority first (00 §4.10). Optional command is the resolved semantic command key for participant wording/ownership; action_key remains the invocation identity. Light item controls supply it.
nodes.name: AdvertisedAction

nodes.description: An authored attribute reference and the actor's current value, which includes allocated levelling points (toolbox row 4) and worn, the nonzero sum its worn items grant (item affects, toolbox row 3; absent when zero).
nodes.name: AttributeView

nodes.description: Current body bleed condition and exact generation for a held bandage invocation.
nodes.name: BleedingView

nodes.description: Confirmed cartridge calendar projection. Phase fields appear only when authored.
nodes.name: CalendarStatus

nodes.description: The highest reached chapter declaration, else the opening chapter (mechanics.md Chapters); derived from the player quest state, never persisted.
nodes.name: ChapterView

nodes.description: One option of a pending choice: choosing it invokes choose with this choice_id.
nodes.name: ChoiceOption

nodes.description: The current encounter and visible opponent presented to the player.
nodes.name: CombatView

nodes.description: One active body status: its authored label, end, next tick and per-tick resource change.
nodes.name: ConditionView

nodes.description: An item inside a container of an EntityView's contents (04 §15 as amended by c1-locks): its id, short name and kind, its direct container (the EntityView's item or another item of the same contents), its state if it has a barrier, and as actions only take and, with a barrier, the container verbs admission and barrier@1 accept now. Optional description is the explicit full-description TextKey; current NPC/item projections always copy their authored definition field, including held/worn/reachable contents. Older snapshots may omit it; the format tag stays.
nodes.name: ContentView

nodes.description: The door (barrier@1) an exit passes through (04 §15 as amended by c1-doors; room-view need #12): its short name, its state, and the door verbs (open, close, lock, unlock) the actor may use on it now, only those admission and the barrier rule would accept, in presentation order. The place's actions never list them.
nodes.name: DoorView

nodes.description: Bed-local saved checkpoint; safe exact offers never replace ordinary World or dialogue.
nodes.name: DreamView

nodes.description: A visible entity (04 §14): the view model, never internal component state. Only entities the actor's AudiencePolicy admits appear (03 §6). An item with a barrier (c1-locks) carries its state and lists the container verbs (open, close, lock, unlock) admission and barrier@1 accept now, each with the item's scope as its entity target and no input. An item without a barrier or with an open one carries contents when it holds an item: every item inside it in reach (containment@1 custody), at any depth, flattened in DefinitionRefString order (a schema may not refer to itself), never an NPC's possessions. Optional description is the explicit full-description TextKey; current NPC/item projections always copy their authored definition field, including held/worn/reachable contents. Older snapshots may omit it; the format tag stays.
nodes.name: EntityView

nodes.description: One exit of the current place (04 §14, §15 as amended by c1-doors; 00 §4.10 compass: disabled when unavailable, badge when locked), with the typed reason when moving through it is not legal now; the door it passes through, also when passable, and what is seen through it unless its door bars the way, also when the move is unaffordable.
nodes.name: ExitView

nodes.description: Confirmed remaining fuel, capacity and effective lit state for the exact item; the presenter computes no elapsed burn.
nodes.name: FuelView

nodes.description: One actor's semantic view (04 §14, §15): the current logical time (to build wait until, P5), the place, its exits, place-level actions, visible entities with their actions, the actor's inventory, quest journal, the body's resources (resource@1; absent when the cartridge has none, an optional field: the snapshot format stays), and the pending choice when one is open. The fields the R6P touch path needs (00 §4.10; P5); the worn equipment, one entry per slot holder (equipment@1; absent when the world has none, an optional field); the actor's position (position@1; absent without it). Map, shop and other surfaces join with their capabilities.
nodes.name: GameView

nodes.description: An authoritative GameView snapshot (04 §16). format versions the envelope: an optional field added to the view keeps the tag; a field made required, removed or reinterpreted takes a new one (the CompiledCartridge ruling, R5 S1 F3/A7). projection_sequence orders this client stream's projection messages; a gap means resync from a fresh snapshot. view_freshness_token is opaque, echoed in ActionInvocation (same 1-128 character limit) for staleness diagnosis. Neither equals an authority revision (04 §16). Incremental projection messages are added with the Realm transport. narration holds committed narration records the client has not yet acknowledged, oldest first; the acknowledgement protocol is deferred to the Realm transport.
nodes.name: GameViewSnapshot

nodes.description: A known directed exit between visited rooms; carries no live traversal availability.
nodes.name: KnownConnectionView

nodes.description: A currently visible NPC or one previously observed by this actor, offered for exact-ID Where.
nodes.name: KnownNpcView

nodes.description: An actor’s visited room with its title and static drawing coordinates.
nodes.name: KnownRoomView

nodes.description: The actor’s visited places and connections between visited endpoints.
nodes.name: MapView

nodes.description: The committed narration of one accepted command, as this actor sees it: the lines of that command's DecisionResult narration (decision.schema.json), keyed by its command_id (06 §43: required narration is committed with its consequence as a stable record of pinned text keys and bindings; 04 §5.2 steps 7-8). Redisplay is read-only. A retry of that command replays its receipt and returns this same record with a current GameView (06 §43; 03 §14).
nodes.name: NarrationRecord

nodes.description: Current-room board identity, title, selected description and ordered notice membership; no bodies.
nodes.name: NoticeBoardView

nodes.description: Current-room readable detail identity, authored page title and selected description; no body. Optional actions list exact-subject readable-detail recipes, exclusively on this Notice, with ordinary availability/reasons and no fabricated command targets.
nodes.name: NoticeView

nodes.description: The actor's open choice (04 §15 'dialogue choices currently available'; 06 §43): its prompt (the line or scene text shown above the options), the speaking participant when there is one, the options in presentation order, and whether the player may close it without choosing (the close_choice command; 06 §43: never trapped in a modal screen, and closing does not change the outcome).
nodes.name: PendingChoice

nodes.description: The current place (04 §14 room).
nodes.name: PlaceView

nodes.description: A journal entry (04 §15 'quest journal state'; 00 §4.10 Journal). Optional journal is the selected TextKey iff its definition declares journal (mechanics.md quest@1).
nodes.name: QuestView

nodes.description: One of the viewer's body's resources (04 §15 as amended 2026-10-01 and 2026-10-02; 21 §4 Resource): its current value at the view's time, its maximum, its condition band key and the band's tone, which the kernel computes from the band table in effect (the pool's bands, else the cartridge's world.bands, else the 04 §15 default table); the UI never computes a threshold (00 §4.10).
nodes.name: ResourceView

nodes.description: Present iff a modal scene runs: its current narrate TextKey, one-based index and narrate count.
nodes.name: SceneView

nodes.description: Current exact keyed provider quote, declared capped benefit and shared availability; no reservation.
nodes.name: ServiceOffer

nodes.description: The current quoted price and availability of one Buy or Sell exchange, with a typed refusal reason when unavailable (B3).
nodes.name: ShopAction

nodes.description: An exact shop item identity and visible name with current Buy and Sell offers; the projection reserves no stock (B3).
nodes.name: ShopItemView

nodes.description: What is seen through an exit whose door does not bar the way (04 §15 as amended by c1-doors; 00 §4.1 scan adjacent rooms): the destination room and its title, and the NPCs and items directly in it, NPCs first, then in DefinitionRefString order. Absent beyond a closed or locked door.
nodes.name: SightView

nodes.description: A skill's permanent acquisition and current qualification as projected for the actor.
nodes.name: SkillView

nodes.description: Exact endpoint route and base quote, effective charge and waiver, and admitted keyed action.
nodes.name: TransportOffer

nodes.description: Why an action, choice or exit is shown but not legal now (00 §4.10: greyed with the reason, badge when locked; P5 'clear unavailable-action feedback'): the typed code, and optionally the player-facing sentence that tells apart two reasons with one code (a locked door, a causeway under the tide). A GameView presentation field, so GameError and the error registry stay unchanged.
nodes.name: UnavailableReason

nodes.description: One equipment slot holder of the actor's body (equipment@1; 04 §14 as amended by c1-equipment): its slot and, when an item is worn there, that item with the actions it accepts (only those resolving to remove). Listed in slot-key order, one entry per place: the finger holder has two (toolbox row 3).
nodes.name: WornSlotView

nodes.description: The current serialized mutation-ownership domain (03 §6). Distinct from WorldContextId: one logical world can hold many authority domains. Lowercase hyphenated UUID, any version.
nodes.name: AuthorityDomainId

nodes.description: A cartridge identity (05 §3 id, 05 §4), lowercase snake_case, at most 64 characters.
nodes.name: CartridgeId

nodes.description: A character (02 §4); the id of player StateScope and player AudiencePolicy (03 §6). Lowercase hyphenated UUID, any version.
nodes.name: CharacterId

nodes.description: Stable semantic Command id (04 §3), derived from the logical idempotency scope and the InvocationId; stable when the AuthorityDomainId changes (03 §6). Lowercase hyphenated UUID, any version.
nodes.name: CommandId

nodes.description: Globally stable, immutable reference to a content definition (03 §2; 05 §4: no global content-key namespace). cartridge_id, kind and key are lowercase snake_case of at most 64 characters; cartridge_version is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without leading zeros, pre-release or build metadata.
nodes.name: DefinitionRef

nodes.description: Canonical string form of a DefinitionRef, cartridge_id@cartridge_version:kind/key (03 §2, 05 §4), with the same segment rules: each at most 64 characters, so every valid DefinitionRef has a valid string form.
nodes.name: DefinitionRefString

nodes.description: Runtime entity identity (03 §3). Two entities from one DefinitionRef have different EntityIds. Lowercase hyphenated UUID, any version.
nodes.name: EntityId

nodes.description: Client-visible stable retry identity of one ActionInvocation (04 §1, §2). Lowercase hyphenated UUID, any version.
nodes.name: InvocationId

nodes.description: A party; the id of party StateScope and party AudiencePolicy (03 §6). Lowercase hyphenated UUID, any version.
nodes.name: PartyId

nodes.description: The broader persistent Realm identity (03 §6); the id of realm StateScope. Lowercase hyphenated UUID, any version.
nodes.name: RealmId

nodes.description: A release version (05 §3 version, §12): MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH without leading zeros, pre-release or build metadata, at most 64 characters.
nodes.name: ReleaseVersion

nodes.description: Logical world/context identity: the simulation, save or deployment context in which state exists (03 §6, 'Logical world identity is not mutation-owner placement'). Never a fencing, owner or shard token. Lowercase hyphenated UUID, any version.
nodes.name: WorldContextId

nodes.description: One Realm placement/routing identity for an authority domain (03 §6). Player and party scope are not permanently owned by it. Lowercase hyphenated UUID, any version.
nodes.name: ZoneShardId

nodes.description: One entry of protocol/invariants.json. citation names a docs/archive/spec/ document and one of its exact heading lines (the contract-links.json convention); a test requires both to exist. implemented_in is where a check by this id runs today (test/loka/core/registries_test.exs holds it to the code): elixir_and_typescript, Loka.Core.Invariants.check/2 and its twin kernel/ts/src/invariants.ts check, on composition and commit observations (protocol/fixtures/composition.json); typescript, only the TypeScript kernel (TypeScript-first rules, ADR-074), kernel/ts/src/world.ts holds on a world or kernel/ts/src/invariants.ts check on one step's observation, run by the simulator (kernel/ts/test/sim.ts); none, no check by id yet, whatever the code and tests enforce (the slice that adds one sets the value; docs/ROADMAP.md plans it).

nodes.name: InvariantEntry

nodes.description: Cartridge-owned mass, integer serving and unit labels for a declared liquid.
nodes.name: LiquidDefinition

nodes.description: Exact vessel contents: null iff zero, positive declared kind bounded by immutable capacity.
nodes.name: LiquidRow

nodes.description: Confirmed vessel contents and authored capacity/labels, never an optimistic amount.
nodes.name: LiquidView

nodes.description: Opted finite vessel shell with authored positive capacity and initial contents.
nodes.name: VesselSpec

nodes.description: api_version: the authored source document/schema family (05 §3).
nodes.name: ApiVersion

nodes.description: A campaign identity (07 §15), lowercase snake_case, at most 64 characters.
nodes.name: CampaignId

nodes.description: A versioned campaign manifest (07 §15, 05 §23): the exact cartridge releases a save lineage composes, at least one. An expansion changes this manifest, never an existing artifact.
nodes.name: CampaignManifest

nodes.description: A cartridge's manifest (05 §3, §20): identity, title, compatibility requirements and supported profiles (at least one; order and duplicates carry no meaning). Fields that freeze with their feature (entry, locales, activation groups, continuity, time policy) are added then (14 §R3B).

nodes.name: CartridgeManifest

nodes.description: An exact immutable cartridge release: cartridge_id@version names exactly one semantic hash (05 §12).
nodes.name: CartridgeRelease

nodes.description: A presentation/input capability of the installed Loka app (05 §3 client_features), lowercase snake_case, at most 64 characters.
nodes.name: ClientFeature

nodes.description: requires (05 §3): a kernel_api range, exact rule_ir and content_schema versions (published cartridges pin them exactly), exact capability versions and required client features. protocol_version is Realm-only and not here (05 §3 'Version vocabulary').
nodes.name: CompatibilityRequirements

nodes.description: A semantic content hash: SHA-256 as 64 lowercase hex digits. It covers the semantic payload only, never signatures, certificates or package bytes (05 §11 'Hash domains and attestations'); how the payload is formed is the compiler's (R4).
nodes.name: ContentHash

nodes.description: How one exact cartridge release is hosted (05 §22): its profile and the exact capability lock it runs (05 §6: deployments pin exact capability versions). Hosting-policy and semantic overlays, each separately hashed and certified, are added when specified.
nodes.name: DeploymentManifest

nodes.description: A hosting profile a cartridge supports or a deployment uses: the canonical execution-profile vocabulary (07 §3; 09 §20 reuses it).
nodes.name: ExecutionProfile

nodes.description: The kernel_api compatibility range a cartridge declares (05 §3 'Compatibility versions'): at_least inclusive, below exclusive, so '>=1.3 <2.0' is at_least 1.3, below 2.0.
nodes.name: KernelApiRange

nodes.description: A kernel_api version, MAJOR.MINOR without leading zeros (05 §3).
nodes.name: KernelApiVersion

nodes.description: Opt-in M1-A elapsed logical seconds per real second; absence retains legacy play_time. Requires kernel API >=1.1 and schedule@1. Millisecond conversion and fractional remainder belong to host M1-B. Integer type obeys loka-numeric-v1 safe range.
nodes.name: TimePolicy

nodes.description: One agent's work on one pull request: its role, model (opus, fable, astra, ...), instance (1, 2, ... among that role's agents on the pull request, so (pull_request, role, instance) is unique), the tokens it used (a required Measure; unknown when not reported, never 0) and the pull request's disposition (merged or closed), which is not a judgment of the agent's work. Evidence for analysis, never an acceptance authority.
nodes.name: AgentWork

nodes.description: The composition-profile limit a decision with genuine ReplayIds exhausted, its result the fault budget_exceeded (04 §5.4): exactly one key of conformance/composition-profile.json limits, the first in that order when several run out at one check. Non-authoritative: never read back as decision input or kept as game state (04 §5.5). 04 §5.5's source and causal values join later as optional fields (ADR-075 §7).
nodes.name: BudgetExceeded

nodes.description: The correlation ids of a content diagnostic: the source revision; input_digest, the SHA-256 of the input the producer read (the compiler: the canonical JSON object mapping each source file's cartridge-relative path to the SHA-256 of its bytes; the loader: the artifact file's bytes; the known answer arrives with the first producer), which exists even when the input does not parse; and content_hash only once an artifact's cartridge hash exists, never a stand-in for it.
nodes.name: BuildIds

nodes.description: What happened to the command's commit (04 §5.1; 03 §14, §15): committed at revision (the revision after; a rejection receipt does not advance it) with the committed events in order and the effect ids; failed (definitively rolled back) with its cause: injected (by the run's fault schedule) or storage_error (the store reported failure; host detail goes to operations); unknown (the outcome could not be observed; reconciled under 03 §15, never presumed rolled back) with its cause: injected or no_outcome (no answer from the store: crash, kill, lost acknowledgement); or unavailable (not_applicable: nothing was committed, such as a fault or a rejection without a receipt). Failed and unknown carry no events or effects: proposed events never leave a failed commit (04 §5.1). The allowed decision and commit pairs: ADR-075 §4.
nodes.name: CommitOutcome

nodes.description: An event or metric name (11 §12): two or three lowercase snake_case segments joined by dots, area first. The registered names are protocol/event_registry.json, which must equal the ObservationRecord branches.
nodes.name: EventName

nodes.description: One entry of protocol/event_registry.json: a name, its store, whether it is an event or a metric (a metric's data is a Measure; the description gives its unit), and a description citing the spec and naming its producers.
nodes.name: EventRegistryEntry

nodes.description: The correlation ids of an operations record: the code revision, the host kind, and the run and command the measure joins (the trace carries the rest).
nodes.name: HostIds

nodes.description: Which host ran the code: a kind, never a device identity (AGENTS.md: no serials, UDIDs or device names).
nodes.name: HostKind

nodes.description: A registered invariant (protocol/invariants.json id) that failed after the command in ids (09 §2 expected and observed invariant: the invariant is the expectation; the record is the observed failure).
nodes.name: InvariantFailure

nodes.description: The source revision that produced a record (11 §11 kernel version; 09 §2 engine/kernel revision): the kernel id (kernel/ts/src/index.ts KERNEL_ID), @, and the full git commit; kernel, compiler and hosts build from one commit. The bare form only from a clean tree at that commit; a tree with uncommitted changes appends -dirty, and such a record is never an exact repro key. Reporting HEAD for a dirty tree is forbidden. It names source, not a fingerprint of a built artifact.
nodes.name: KernelVersion

nodes.description: One word of a failed lookup as the producer recorded it: the normalized word (lowercase letters and digits, at most 32), or redacted when it held a host identifier (ADR-075 §6) or anything else a record may not carry. Redaction happens before the record is built; a redacted word is marked, never an empty string.
nodes.name: LookupWord

nodes.description: A measured quantity, never a bare number: observed with a non-negative integer value, unknown (it applies but could not be observed; never 0), or unavailable with its cause (never empty or absent).
nodes.name: Measure

nodes.description: The format tag of every observation record. A new field or meaning takes a new tag.
nodes.name: ObservationFormat

nodes.description: Every observation record, one per JSON Lines line in canonical encoding (ADR-075 §1): the format tag, the registered event name, its store, the store's closed correlation ids and the event's data. One branch per protocol/event_registry.json entry.
nodes.name: ObservationRecord

nodes.description: The store a record belongs to (ADR-075 §2): game_trace (per-command decisions, host-independent, 11 §15), diagnostics (things to fix: 08 §6 diagnostics and simulator failures), operations (host timings, 11 §13), dev_evidence (agent work cost and outcome).
nodes.name: ObservationStore

nodes.description: The correlation ids of a record that must reproduce by deterministic replay (09 §2): the cartridge hash, the code revision, the run's initial RNG state, the run (the durable local save run; for CLI/simulator producers, their independent execution or sequence run), the command, and the authority revision the command was decided against. Local ids only: no host, device, account or time.
nodes.name: ReplayIds

nodes.description: One bounded uniform draw (09 §4 draw trace; numeric profile): its bound and the value drawn, value below bound.
nodes.name: RngDraw

nodes.description: The RNG draws of an accepted decision, in draw order (11 §15 'RNG draws if configured'; 09 §4): observed (draws [] is a decision that drew nothing), unknown (collection was on but could not supply a complete list), or unavailable (not_collected: collection was off).
nodes.name: RngTrace

nodes.description: The replay header of one run (09 §2; ADR-075 §4), written once before its first trace.command: world_context_id, the logical world the run's fresh state and every id are minted in (so a run with no commands still reconstructs its initial world; ADR-075 amendment 2026-09-25, R5 S1 review A4); with its ids (cartridge, source revision, seed, run) and the ordered commands of the run's trace.command entries, the complete replay input. initial_state: fresh (the cartridge's initial state) or unavailable, not_collected (a start from a snapshot, whose identity is not recorded until R6 checkpoints define one). fault_schedule: the SHA-256 of the canonical fault schedule R6 fault simulation defines, or unavailable (not_applicable) when none is injected.
nodes.name: RunHeader

nodes.description: The correlation ids of a run header, and of a failed lookup in that run (target.unresolved): the replay inputs a run shares (ReplayIds without command and revision).
nodes.name: RunIds

nodes.description: A player's lookup that resolved to no target or to several (21 §7 none | ambiguous; 04 §18), so no Command was built and nothing reached the game_trace (owner request, R5 S2: the Lab, bots and tests see what players try that the content lacks). room: the room it was tried in; outcome and candidates: the resolution and its candidate count (0 for none); words: the normalized words compared, after redaction, at most 16; after_ordinal: the ordinal of the run's last trace.command before it (0 before the first), joining it to the game_trace by run_id.
nodes.name: TargetUnresolved

nodes.description: The decision outcome of a traced command (DecisionResult, 04 §5), compact: accepted with its typed outcome, the state delta digest (SHA-256 of the canonical bytes of its StateDelta, the content_hash construction; its known answer arrives with the first producer), its RNG draws and the RNG state it returned (DecisionResult.rng; the delta does not cover it); rejected with its GameError; or fault with its ErrorCode and, when bound, its target (04 §5.5).
nodes.name: TraceDecision

nodes.description: One game-trace entry (11 §15; 09 §7): its ordinal (1, 2, ... in the run's command order, binding it to the run's trace.run header), the full Command (command.id equals ids.command_id), the decision, and the commit outcome, for accepted and rejected decisions and failed commits alike. Derived, never authority. No time, duration, host or device field: entries are identical across hosts given identical complete replay inputs and controlled faults (ADR-075 §4).
nodes.name: TraceEntry

nodes.description: Why a value is unavailable: not_applicable (it does not apply here, such as a commit for a fault), not_collected (collection is off, such as RNG draws when the draw trace is not configured).
nodes.name: UnavailableCause

nodes.description: The correlation id of a dev-evidence record: the pull request of the work on lorecrafting/lokacore.
nodes.name: WorkIds

nodes.description: A pure condition tree (06 §21). all/any/not compose; the leaves are the 06 §21 operators the R6P proof uses (pre-release-proof.md) and the rest are added with their first use, each versioned by its owning capability (VersionedPolicy). fact_compare compares FactValue. stat_compare and resource_compare (attributes@1, 06 §21 amendment 2026-10-03) hold when the actor's attribute value, or the current value of the resource on the actor's body, is at least at_least; below is not, a range is all.
nodes.name: Policy

nodes.description: Persisted QuestInstance lifecycle state (06 §1). Availability is derived, not a state.
nodes.name: QuestState

nodes.description: A policy tree with the AST version it was written against (14 §R3A 'core policy AST/versioning'). A new leaf operator is versioned by its owning capability, which the cartridge must lock (capability_registry.json policies); adding an operator to a capability version that is already installed takes that capability's next version. A changed meaning of an existing operator takes a new policy_version.
nodes.name: VersionedPolicy

nodes.description: A quest with one objective (06 §2; R6P pre-release-proof.md), keyed in CompiledCartridge.quests by DefinitionRefString of kind quest, owned by quest@1 (a cartridge with one requires it): its key, also the stable action key of its offer (no action's, recipe's or registered command's: DUPLICATE_DEFINITION); title, the text key of its journal entry (QuestView.title); offer, optional, the accept action its actor's ActionSet lists while the actor has no instance of the quest (label its text key, policy its availability: while it fails the offer is shown unavailable and accept_quest is rejected), which resolves to accept_quest; without one, only a dialogue choice's accept (dialogue.schema.json DialogueChoice) activates the quest; and objective (QuestObjective). Resolution is another capability's: a choice resolves it through quest@1's resolution, which re-checks the objective. Giver, turn-in, prerequisites beyond the offer's policy, further objectives, outcomes and automatic or discovered activation join as optional fields. Optional journal declares lifecycle texts (QuestJournal); selection is computed in QuestView without changing persisted state.
nodes.name: QuestDefinition

nodes.description: Lifecycle journal texts, selected by quest@1 in GameView (06 §2, §41; 04 §15, c1-journal amendment). All five stage texts are required; outcomes optionally overrides terminal text by outcome key. Outcome keys need not name a dialogue choice. Reveal and hints remain LATER. API1.9 active_variants are checked in order for active quests; the first holding policy supplies text, otherwise ordinary active/objectives_met selection applies.
nodes.name: QuestJournal

nodes.description: A quest's one objective and its evidence policy (06 §3 Objective credit/causation policy, §43; 04 §5.2). current_state: met while policy holds for the actor, evaluated on the state at hand and never stored (the R6P lantern: current possession, so a lantern taken before acceptance counts and one given away no longer does). post_activation_event: met by an item_acquired event whose item is the item `item_acquired` names and whose holder is the actor's body, at a causal position after the instance's activation; the instance then moves to objectives_complete in the same decision, and an acquisition before activation never counts (the Tiny fixture's strict credit; its automatic resolution is not part of this vocabulary yet).
nodes.name: QuestObjective

nodes.description: Typed reaction owned by reaction@1. Fact and room triggers retain the command actor; quest resolution verifies the source instance. Apply may assign facts or activate a quest on quest_resolved. API1.12 adds typed quest.resolve and quest.fail on fact_changed. Deliveries use one writer group and the existing FIFO budgets; faults commit nothing.
nodes.name: ReactionRule

nodes.description: One bounded crow slot's exact scavenging occurrence. Idle rows retain the last member generation without a pending item or job.
nodes.name: CrowTransport

nodes.description: A runtime entity's identity and provenance (03 §3, §11; 21 §4): its own id, the definition it instantiates (never the definition record itself), its origin, and for a player/party overlay entity its StateScope and AudiencePolicy; shared entities omit both. Authority revision is host metadata.
nodes.name: EntityIdentity

nodes.description: Where a runtime entity came from (21 §4 'spawn/population provenance'; 05 §25 'Population provenance': a plan may only replenish or clean up what it spawned).
nodes.name: EntityOrigin

nodes.description: API1.11 escort@1 relation, keyed by actor_id. Identity is immutable; only status changes through escort.transition. The original continuation and choice bind the selected NPC and active quest instance.
nodes.name: EscortRelation

nodes.description: The bounded escort lifecycle: following moves with the actor, separated waits for explicit rejoin, completed never follows again.
nodes.name: EscortStatus

nodes.description: One player's current bounded expedition attempt, bound to its quest instance.
nodes.name: ExpeditionAttempt

nodes.description: The exact quest instance, accepted attempt, occurrence cursor and lifecycle drawn on a patrol control; a fresh invocation cannot reuse a stale leg.
nodes.name: PatrolDraw

nodes.description: Quest-instance-keyed original leader attempt: immutable actor/body/NPC/activation identity, accepted command attempt, bounded cursor/unique checkpoint credit and explicit recovery lifecycle.
nodes.name: PatrolRelation

nodes.description: Together, awaiting ordinary player entry, explicitly paused, fatally failed or terminally completed.
nodes.name: PatrolStatus

nodes.description: Current plan job and next wander boundary; membership resides only in fixed slots.
nodes.name: PopulationControl

nodes.description: One fixed ordinal population slot. A dead member remains bound until a later eligible replacement.
nodes.name: PopulationSlot

nodes.description: A typed, capability-owned relation between runtime entities (21 §4 'Typed relations'; Loka is not an untyped graph). One branch per kind in use: containment (containment@1), an entity's one container (03 §23). Equipment, ownership, custody, membership, following, participation and relationship links join as branches with their owning capability.
nodes.name: Relation

nodes.description: A condition band table (04 §15 as amended 2026-10-02), highest cut first: the band is the first row whose cut p reaches, and maximum = minimum gives the top row. Cuts are strictly descending and the last is 0, so every value has a band, and keys are unique within the table; the compiler and loader report a table that breaks this as RESOURCE_SPEC_INVALID at the table. A pool's bands (ResourceSpec), else the cartridge's world.bands (cartridge.schema.json WorldSettings), else the engine default table.
nodes.name: BandTable

nodes.description: A condition band's tone (04 §15 as amended 2026-10-02): how serious the band is; each presenter maps it to its own colour.
nodes.name: BandTone

nodes.description: One row of a condition band table: the band key holds when p, the percentage of the pool's range from its minimum, reaches at_percent (in integers: 100 x (current - minimum) >= at_percent x (maximum - minimum)). key is a content Key whose text is band.<key> in the catalog when the cartridge authors it; tone is how serious it is.
nodes.name: ConditionBand

nodes.description: Explicit entity-specific HP bounds/start/gain. Requires kernel API 1.4; minimum <= start <= maximum (RESOURCE_SPEC_INVALID). Required legacy-shaped birth/save row; no position recovery.
nodes.name: NpcHp

nodes.description: A resource bound, value or amount: a 32-bit signed integer, so that every derived value (regeneration, costs, adjustments) stays exact in every kernel's arithmetic.
nodes.name: ResourceInt

nodes.description: Optional exact fractional recovery by stored position rate. Requires position@1, real_elapsed and the recovery API. Compiler/loader additionally require every <= floor(MAX_SAFE/(maximum authored rate+1)).
nodes.name: ResourceRegen

nodes.description: A typed bounded integer resource each body holds (21 §4 Resource), keyed in CompiledCartridge.resources by DefinitionRefString of kind resource: inclusive bounds minimum <= start <= maximum (RESOURCE_SPEC_INVALID otherwise), start its value on a new body, and gain its legacy regeneration per authored gain_every interval: each crossed interval boundary adds gain, stopping at maximum; that stop is the regeneration rule, never a clamp of an adjustment (delta.schema.json resource.adjust). The value is derived, never ticked (02 derived state): it is stored only when written. A body's resources belong to the body, not the character driving it (owner decision on puppeting). Keys hp, ma and mv are the engine's default pools (00 §4 amendment, DikuMUD): the compiler adds them to every loka-cartridge-v2 cartridge, with resource@1 and schedule@1 (whose wait lets an exhausted body regenerate), as hp 0..20 start 20 gain 5, ma 0..100 start 100 gain 4 and mv 0..82 start 82 gain 18, each field overridable in the source's resources.json; mv is the pool a move pays 1 from (movement@1), in a cartridge that declares it, unless the cartridge's world.movement.cost (cartridge.schema.json WorldSettings) names another cost. bands, when present, is this pool's condition band table (BandTable); absent, the pool takes the cartridge's world.bands, else the engine default table (04 §15 as amended 2026-10-02). The compiler writes bands only where the source authors them. resource@1 emits no events. Optional regen replaces hourly gain with exact fractional elapsed settlement using the old stored rate; queries never write. See active mechanics.md resource@1 and protocol.md Composition.
nodes.name: ResourceSpec

nodes.description: A word or phrase a player types to name a detail (21 §6 aliases; 04 §18 aliases) or, for an ActionRecipe, the action (its verb, the first words typed): lowercase letters and digits, the words of a phrase joined by _ (the player's `mooring post` is compared as mooring_post; kernel/ts/src/target.ts gives the normalization). At most 64 characters.
nodes.name: Alias

nodes.description: Shared mutable state for one logical door or gate (21 §5 Barrier), owned by barrier@1 (a cartridge with one requires it), keyed in CompiledCartridge.barriers by DefinitionRefString of kind barrier and named by the exits that pass through it (Connection.barrier): its key; keywords, the Alias words a player names it by after open, close, lock or unlock (the direction of its exit names it too); short, the text key of its short description ("the oak door"); initial, its state in a fresh world (BarrierState); and optionally key_item, the item whose holder may lock and unlock it (has_item: held directly or inside containers the holder holds). Without key_item no one can lock or unlock it. Damaged/repaired and blocked states join as optional fields. Optional tags are its property tags (entity.schema.json Tag, toolbox row G1).
nodes.name: BarrierDefinition

nodes.description: A barrier's state (21 §5 Barrier: open/closed, locked/unlocked): open, closed (and unlocked) or locked (and closed); a lock needs a closed door, so an open locked barrier does not exist. The legal transitions (04 §5.3 'Lifecycle transition') are closed to open (open), open to closed (close), closed to locked (lock) and locked to closed (unlock); delta.schema.json barrier.transition.
nodes.name: BarrierState

nodes.description: One directed exit to another room of the same cartridge (21 §5 Connection; 05 §17). Its identity is its room and direction. barrier, optional (barrier@1), names the Barrier whose one shared state the exit passes through (21 §5 Barrier; 05 §25 coherent connections): move through it is refused while it is closed (exit_closed) or locked (exit_locked); an exit without one means what it always meant. A reciprocal exit is authored in the destination room (00a §2); faces pair by opposite direction: an exit's reciprocal face is its destination's exit in the opposite compass direction when that exit leads back to its room, and an exit with a barrier needs a reciprocal face naming the same barrier (BARRIER_MISMATCH at each face otherwise). One-way and bent barrier passages (no reciprocal face, or an opposite-direction exit that leads elsewhere) are rejected for now and may be allowed later; an exit without a barrier is BARRIER_MISMATCH only when its reciprocal face names one.
nodes.name: Connection

nodes.description: Prose selected by a condition (21 §6 DescriptionVariant; 00a §12): description replaces the base description key when the condition holds for the actor over committed state (policy.schema.json VersionedPolicy; the evaluator is pure, 06 §21). A room's or detail's variants are tried in list order and the first whose condition holds is shown; when none holds, the base description is. Variants are derived, never a mutated description (21 §6). Owned by description_variant (a cartridge with one requires it); its condition's ops by their owners.
nodes.name: DescriptionVariant

nodes.description: A lightweight keyed detail of a room (21 §6 InspectableDetail): the aliases a player can name it by, the first of which also names it when a lookup is ambiguous, and its description text key (05 §18). Not a RuntimeEntity: a fresh world gives it a target id only (numeric profile, Initial world ids). Two details of one room may share an alias (an ambiguous lookup lists both, 04 §18), but the first alias must be the detail's own and in the form a lookup produces (no empty word, not starting with at, the, a or an), or the player could not pick it by name (UNREACHABLE_DETAIL). Its variants (DescriptionVariant) select other prose by condition. Owned by inspectable_detail (a cartridge with details requires it). R5 freezes this v1 shape (14 §R5): perception, reveal facts and contextual actions join as optional fields.
nodes.name: InspectableDetail

nodes.description: A local barrier face’s authored answer when the named NPC is in the destination room, and its no-answer text.
nodes.name: KnockResponse

nodes.description: A navigable place (21 §5 Place/Room): its key, its title and description text keys (05 §18; resolved in the cartridge text catalog), and its exits by compass direction, the six-way compass of 00 §4.10 (a direction without an exit is absent), optionally its inspectable details by key, at most 64, its description variants (DescriptionVariant) and its contributions to the ActionSet of an actor in it, applied in order (action.schema.json ActionContribution; R5 S5, optional). Custom named connections (05 §17) join later as a separate optional field. Optional tags are its property tags (entity.schema.json Tag, toolbox row G1).
nodes.name: RoomDefinition

nodes.description: Captured original scene-owned choice occurrence at its shown choice beat.
nodes.name: DreamDraw

nodes.description: One exact paid Rest binding: authored bed, first-credit fact and sole quest.
nodes.name: RestBinding

nodes.description: Modal narration or the consumed paid-Rest anchored, resumable presentation-only dream.
nodes.name: SceneDefinition

nodes.description: The installed closed scene step subset; no arbitrary writes.
nodes.name: SceneStep

nodes.description: Who may perceive or interact with a runtime entity or projection, independent of state ownership (03 §6, 'Audience / visibility policy'). Governs GameView inclusion, target resolution, interaction and narration; the authority rejects actors outside it.
nodes.name: AudiencePolicy

nodes.description: Who owns or experiences a gameplay truth (03 §6). Exactly one of player, party, instance or realm, each with its typed id. There is no default: a missing kind or id is invalid, never realm (03 §6). Scope is not authority placement.
nodes.name: StateScope

nodes.description: Closed paid entitlement, finite meal recovery or provider-owned complete liquid serving; recovery is MV only.
nodes.name: ServiceBenefit

nodes.description: Exact original-provider action and conserved quote with one typed immediate benefit.
nodes.name: ServiceDefinition

nodes.description: Localized text: a string id and its named bindings (04 §15 'localized string IDs plus interpolation data'; 06 §43 'pinned text keys and bindings'). Binding names are lowercase snake_case, at most 64 characters. Participants: the entities a committed line names, each pinned to its EntityId when the line commits (06 §43 'pinned text keys and bindings', 'bound participant identities'), so redisplay never resolves them again; names are lowercase snake_case, at most 64 characters.
nodes.name: Text

nodes.description: The cartridge's default-locale strings (05 §18: stable string ids, inline defaults extracted into a catalog): each TextKey to its display text, 1 to 4,096 characters. One locale only; per-locale catalogs, plural rules and binding placeholders join later under a new cartridge format tag. Every text key a room, detail, variant, item, NPC (short, room_line, description) or action (label, accessibility) uses has an entry; a string marks its tappable words inline as touch links (owner decision 2026-09-25, Q3): the words in square brackets, which link the thing whose text it is, optionally followed at once by a target key in parentheses, which links that detail of the room or item or NPC of the cartridge instead (DiagnosticCode UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE, TOUCH_LINK_MISSING), so each locale marks its own words; a host showing plain text shows the words without the brackets and target; the compiler and loader report a missing one as UNRESOLVED_REFERENCE.

nodes.description: A localization string id, never display text (04 §15; 05 §18): lowercase dotted snake_case of at most 128 characters, the ActionDefinition label rule. Text carries its interpolation bindings.
nodes.name: TextKey

nodes.description: A value interpolated into localized text (04 §15 'interpolation data'; 06 §43 'bindings'): a TextKey (localized in turn, so a Key such as a direction also fits), an integer (a count, a time) or a boolean.
nodes.name: TextValue

nodes.description: Paired original boarding detail, destination, conserved fare recipient and corpse recovery rooms.

nodes.description: One actual owned nonempty underwater corpse currently eligible at the shrine, with its current bottom location and original direct-root identities/names.

nodes.description: One bound water occurrence: exact bottom DefinitionRef, due clock, actor/body/generation and pending, completed or cancelled status. Historical rows remain; only the current occurrence may drown.

nodes.description: One actor-owned body and occupancy generation. Active rows bind bottom, entry clock, absolute deadline and one job. Cleared rows retain generation/body and null all occurrence fields.
nodes.name: WaterOccupancy

nodes.description: D6 exact paired surface/bottom routes, usable skill, entry load/cost, absolute submersion duration and authored warning/death copy; real_elapsed content only.

nodes.description: Confirmed deadline, logical time remaining and real seconds rounded up from the authored elapsed rate. Presentation never advances or renews the deadline.
nodes.name: WaterView
